report:
test_total does not fail. It passes. The test that fails is test_half_cent_rounds_up.

What I ran: python -B -m pytest -q (no files changed). Result: 2 passed, 1 failed.

  FAILED test_cart.py::test_half_cent_rounds_up - assert 959 == 960

Why it fails:
cart.py line 7 does int(subtotal * (1 - discount_percent / 100)).
int() cuts off the fraction. It does not round.
- 1010 cents with 5% off is 959.5. int() gives 959. The test expects 960.
- 399 cents with 10% off is 359.1. int() gives 359. That matches, so test_total passes.

So every discounted total with a fraction is cut down, never rounded up.
This matches the TODO item "customers see totals one cent short".
The docstring says "rounded to whole cents", but the code truncates.

I changed nothing. If you want a fix, tell me which rounding rule you want
(half up, as the test comment says, or another rule) and I will make it.
Note: Python's round() uses banker's rounding (959.5 -> 960, but 958.5 -> 958),
so it is not plain half up.
